answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may place orders. When an agent defaults or is proven to double-spend, the protocol slashes that bond and pays part to the harmed counterparty; creating many identities therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. A wharf may accept saffron bids from a falcon agent, but each account must post its own bond, which stays locked while disputes are resolved.
